question: Should `memory-lancedb` auto-capture reject OpenClaw-authored external-content wrappers by default, or should this be exposed as a new `captureFilter` configuration option?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent fix defines whether untrusted-source memory protection is a default framework security boundary or an operator-controlled policy knob.

options.title: Reject Wrappers By Default
options.body: Treat `EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT` as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for wrapped web, browser, and tool content.

options.title: Add `captureFilter` Config
options.body: Introduce a documented `excludeWrapped` option with schema, manifest metadata, docs, and upgrade-safe default tests.

options.title: Defer To Provenance Design
options.body: Leave this narrow filter open until the broader memory trust/provenance model defines the canonical source-authority contract.

recommendation.title: Reject Wrappers By Default
recommendation.body: Treat `EXTERNAL_UNTRUSTED_CONTENT` as a host-owned capture boundary before trigger matching and add regression coverage for wrapped web, browser, and tool content.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent memory-lancedb maintenance trail and this decision crosses config, memory persistence, and security policy.
